question: Who became the new CEO of Foundation Consumer Healthcare in August 2026?

hits.title: Prestige Consumer Healthcare Inc completes acquisition of Breathe Right(R).
hits.snippet: The closing was finalized pursuant to the terms of the asset purchase agreement, announced on March 20, 2026, under which Prestige agreed to acquire the Breathe Right(R) brand and certain other brands from Foundation Consumer Healthcare for $1.045 billion, or approximately $900 million net of anticipated tax benefits valued at $150 million.

hits.title: Foundation Consumer Healthcare sells portion of consumer health business.
hits.snippet: Through our work with Plan B, FCH continues to make strides to provide education and increase access to emergency contraception for women.

hits.title: Press Release
hits.snippet: Foundation Consumer Healthcare (FCH), the maker of Plan B One‑Step ® 1.5 mg levonorgestrel emergency contraception (Plan B), has been working with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to update the product label to accurately reflect how Plan B works.

hits.title: POWER TO DECIDE TO PARTNER WITH FOUNDATION CONSUMER HEALTHCARE | Power to Decide
hits.snippet: Power to Decide is proud to announce a partnership with Foundation Consumer Healthcare (FCH), the maker of Plan B One-Step® emergency contraception.

hits.title: Foundation Consumer Healthcare's Plan B Contraception Launches Campaign 03/22/2019
hits.snippet: Foundation Consumer Healthcare is launching a national campaign for its Plan B One-Step emergency contraceptive brand.

hits.title: Greg Bradley named Foundation Consumer Healthcare CEO
hits.snippet: Foundation Consumer Healthcare (FCH) has named Greg Bradley president and chief executive officer.

hits.title: Plan B amplifies voice of Republican voters: keep emergency contraception.
hits.snippet: Foundation acquired the brand from Teva in 2017 in a $675 million deal.

accuracy.note: Answer names Greg Bradley, not Rupa Bahri

ar.note: No snippet mentions Rupa Bahri or an August 2026 CEO appointment; rank 6 names a different CEO (Greg Bradley).
